name: Axe Compute Inc.
role: GPU compute provider: Access capacity services and Build owned-cluster delivery
overview: Axe supplies enterprise GPU compute through Access and dedicated Build infrastructure. Its legacy Helomics business was sold and is reported as discontinued operations. Current recognized compute revenue, signed future contracts and customer-funded delivery obligations have different scopes. Georgia hardware is owned through an acquired SPV while Duos owns/operates the facility; technical provisioning has not established customer acceptance or Build revenue commencement.

size.label: Size unverified
size.basis: Current common-equity/prefunded-warrant economics and later changes are unreconciled. A separately displayed dated provider headline does not establish independently validated capitalization or a debt/market-cap denominator. The September 2025 reverse split is already reflected in 2026 filing counts.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — identity and current share count
sources.excerpt: AXE COMPUTE INC.; trading symbol AGPU. As of November 13, 2026, 13,650,314 common shares were outstanding. The quarterly reporting period ended September 30, 2026. The company describes GPU compute services and owned GPU infrastructure; the Helomics sale closed September 11, 2026.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 results — revenue and earnings scope
sources.excerpt: Three months ended September 30, 2026: revenue $7,243,043; operating income $6,825,897, including gains on digital assets of $10,477,971. All revenue was delivered under Access; Build revenue begins upon deployment. Adjusted EBITDA was $(2,275) thousand in the issuer non-GAAP reconciliation, not positive operating cash earnings.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — September balance sheet
sources.excerpt: September 30, 2026 balance sheet: cash and cash equivalents $147,710,376; note payable $291,722; deferred purchase price payable, net of discount $36,597,577. Current/noncurrent operating lease liabilities were $15,470,820/$14,435,540. Current/noncurrent contract liabilities were $100,881,687/$468,457,286.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — Note 4 customer concentration
sources.excerpt: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, Customer A represented 22% of revenue and Customer B 58%; for nine months their percentages were 30% and 48%. The customers are not named. Revenue recognized under fixed-term GPU compute contracts represented all reported revenue.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — Note 4 contract balances
sources.excerpt: The contract-liability rollforward reports advance billings $579,796,296, revenue recognized $(10,457,323), and closing contract liabilities $569,338,973. The issuer also identifies $569.3 million of remaining performance obligations: $8,104,000 in the remaining three months of 2026, $129,093,077 in 2027, $127,220,420 in 2028 and $304,921,476 in 2029. These are not additional amounts to add to the same contract-liability balance.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — Georgia deferred purchase financing
sources.excerpt: The deferred purchase price has $42.9 million face amount, $715,000 monthly installments, and all unpaid amounts due by the earlier of September 30, 2027 and a financing secured by the cluster. Duos retains a security interest. It bears no stated interest; $36.6 million present value uses a 17.71% imputed rate over an expected 12-month term. The $6.3 million discount is recognized as interest. Note 8 schedules $2.1 million in remaining 2026 and $40.8 million in 2027, assuming the outside date.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — Note 10 insurance note
sources.excerpt: June 2026 director-and-officer insurance financing requires ten monthly installment payments through April 2027, secured by a first-priority lien on the financed policies. The annual percentage rate is 6.1%; September balance is approximately $0.3 million including interest. The exact balance-sheet note amount is $291,722.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — Note 9 commenced and uncommenced leases
sources.excerpt: Total operating lease liabilities at September 30 were $29,906,360. Separately, total future payments under leases committed to but not yet commenced were $407.4 million, expected to commence in 2026 and 2027 with terms of two to four years. The 12.3% weighted-average discount rate on recognized operating leases is an accounting borrowing-rate assumption, not a corporate loan coupon.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — Note 4 vendor prepayments
sources.excerpt: The issuer recorded $92.7 million of compute prepayments at September 30: $85.6 million for leases not yet commenced and $7.1 million for compute capacity and expenses. These are prepaid vendor assets, not an undrawn credit facility or additional cash balance.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — cash-flow period
sources.excerpt: Net cash provided by continuing operating activities was $465,234,067 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The issuer release attributes the inflow principally to customer prepayments, partly offset by vendor prepayments. The statement is nine-month cumulative; it is not a three-month Q3 cash-flow measure.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 results — Georgia stage and revised roadmap
sources.excerpt: The Georgia cluster consists of 288 Supermicro NVIDIA B300 NVL8 servers containing 2,304 GPUs at a Duos-operated facility with approximately 5 MW of committed power. It was not placed in service at September 30. The cluster is energized and provisioned, with customer acceptance underway. The roadmap states fourth quarter 2026 and first quarter 2027 to complete acceptance and place the cluster into service. All Q3 revenue was Access.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 results — contracts, TCV and future ARR
sources.excerpt: The company reports more than $2.8 billion of July 2026 Build contracts and more than $3 billion of signed total contract value. It expects more than $700 million annualized run rate upon full deployment. The company does not provide formal financial guidance. Signed TCV and full-deployment run rate are not recognized revenue or current operating ARR.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q1 2026 results — original Georgia deployment target
sources.excerpt: The issuer described a 36-month, $260 million enterprise contract for a dedicated 2,304 NVIDIA B300 GPU cluster. Deployment was targeted for Q3 2026, with approximately $21 million of quarterly revenue once live. This was a forward-looking original service-entry target, not completion evidence.

sources.title: Axe Compute acquires Georgia cluster SPV and extends customer term
sources.excerpt: The acquisition of 100% of the Georgia GPU SPV completed September 30, 2026. At closing, approximately $87.8 million of SPV asset-backed financing was paid off with no new equity issued. Remaining consideration was $42.9 million deferred purchase price. The customer agreement was extended from three years to five years through 2031. Duos continues to own and operate the facility; 288 servers contain 2,304 B300 GPUs.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — outstanding shares and prefunded warrants
sources.excerpt: The November 13 cover-page common-share count was 13,650,314. At September 30, 7,736,379 prefunded warrants were outstanding, vested and exercisable without expiration; their $0.01 exercise price causes inclusion in EPS weighted-average common shares. EPS weighted averages are not a current basic common-share count. Preferred stock, other warrants and conversion rights are separate capitalization considerations.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q2 2026 Form 10-Q — reverse-split basis
sources.excerpt: The company completed a one-for-fifteen reverse split on September 29, 2025, effective for trading September 30, 2025. The filing says share and per-share amounts have already been adjusted for the reverse split. Do not apply that split a second time to the 2026 share counts.

sources.title: StockAnalysis AGPU capitalization page — dated provider headline, not reconciled value
sources.excerpt: Fresh page read on November 24 displayed $78.7 million as of November 23, 2026 and a separate historical November 20 row of $77.90 million. Provider metadata still said last updated November 20. The v11 reviewed capture retained $79.4 million for a November 23 intraday headline. Different readings have no verified common valuation time; current prefunded-warrant/share basis remains unresolved.

sources.title: Axe Compute Q3 2026 Form 10-Q — expense and capitalization tables
sources.excerpt: Q3 revenue 7,243,043; cost of revenue 6,911,526. September 30 common shares 13,634,097 and prefunded warrants 7,736,379; prefunded exercise price $0.01. Remaining ATM capacity approximately $83M; other warrants 1,592,749. These are distinct capital instruments, not a fully diluted share total.

sources.title: Axe Compute definitive annual meeting proxy — December 17 vote and proposed equity plan
sources.excerpt: Annual meeting December 17, 2026, 11:00 a.m. Eastern. Proposal 3 adds 2,000,000 plan shares, increasing reserve from 1,066,667 to 3,066,667; annual increases up to 5% begin January 1, 2028 through 2034. Issuer-reported equity award overhang changes from 13.5% to 28.1%, excluding future evergreen increases. Proposed capacity is not current issuance. November 6 common count is 13,650,314.

sources.title: October 5 Georgia acquisition release — amended lifetime revenue expectation
sources.excerpt: Issuer estimates $364.6 million revenue over the customer agreement, extended to five years through 2031. Duos covers facility colocation and energy for that term. Margin improvement is expected, but no numerical gross margin or quarterly revenue schedule is supplied.

questions: When will Georgia customer acceptance be documented, and when will service billing and GAAP Build revenue actually begin? Latest verified issuer status is acceptance underway, not customer accepted.
What is the independently corroborated installation/energization date and operating IT load? Approximately 5 MW committed power cannot be substituted for IT MW or a company fleet total.
How will the secured seller-financing balloon be funded by September 30, 2027, or earlier if cluster financing accelerates it? A refinancing also has to satisfy the existing secured seller claim.
How much reported cash is legally available to the parent versus earmarked by delivery/vendor obligations? Customer prepayments and prepaid vendor assets must not be added to available liquidity.
Can the $407.4M uncommenced lease commitments, existing operating leases, delivery capex and customer prepayments be reconciled into a dated future funding bridge without double counting?
Who are anonymous revenue Customers A and B, and what are their credit, termination, renewal and prepayment protections? Do not infer their identity from future Georgia/Build contracts.

How should the 13,650,314 common shares dated November 13, 7,736,379 prefunded warrants dated September 30, preferred/conversion rights, other warrants and later exercises enter basic versus economic/fully diluted capitalization? Do not use EPS weighted averages.

What evidence supports the difference between the v11 $79.4M and freshly displayed $78.7M provider headlines for the same November 23 intraday date? Exact valuation times are not verified; the size and debt ratio remain withheld.
When will the next earnings call be formally dated? The calendar reread November 24 was accessible and still contained an undated upcoming section and archived November 17 results call.
Can a compatible recast six-month cash-flow statement be established to derive Q3-only operating cash flow and capex? The loaded $465.2M inflow is nine-month and customer-prepayment-driven.

The November 25 review found the November 24 definitive proxy after the prior review cutoff. Will December 17 shareholders approve Proposal 3, and what awards or ATM sales follow? The reviewed SEC submissions list also contains a November 24 annual-report filing; this review does not claim continuous monitoring or a separately verified new operating update from that attachment.
